title: Aku Simon dari Kirene
summary_zh: 我是来自古利内的西门。 我的名字表明我住在非洲大陆。
title_zh: 我是古利奈人西门。
content: Aku Simon dari Kirene. Namaku menunjukkan bahwa aku tinggal di benua Afrika. Meski demikian, kulitku tidak hitam dan bibirku pun tidak tebal. Dan meskipun sudah selama beberapa generasi keluargaku berdiam di Kirene, ibu kota Kireneika -- sebuah kota Yunani di Afrika Utara yang terkenal karena kemakmuran dan para ahli filsafatnya -- kulitku tidaklah putih. Aku Simon dari Kirene. Aku orang Yahudi asli sampai ke jantung hati. Sejak kecil, kutaati semua hukum agama tanpa kecuali, walaupun aku tidak lagi fasih berbahasa Aram akibat dibesarkan dalam masyarakat yang berbahasa Yunani. Aku Simon dari Kirene. Aku tidak ingin berkisah tentang diri sendiri. Juga tidak tentang semua pengalaman hidupku. Aku cuma ingin bercerita tentang pengalamanku yang satu itu. Pengalaman yang kemudian mengubah seluruh jalan hidupku. Dan seluruh jalan hidup Anda, sekiranya Anda juga mengalaminya. Hari itu adalah hari Jumat. Aku baru saja tiba di Yerusalem pagi itu. Tujuanku melakukan perjalanan yang jauh itu adalah untuk merayakan hari raya Paskah. Setiap tahun aku melakukannya. Tidak sedikit pun aku heran melihat orang-orang penuh sesak memadati kota. Walaupun letih, segera setelah menaruh barang-barangku di hotel dan membersihkan badan, aku keluar berjalan-jalan untuk menikmati keriuhan kota yang sedang larut dalam semarak pesta. Lengking jeritan anak-anak yang berlari ria kian kemari, teriakan membujuk bahkan kadang-kadang memaksa para pedagang yang menjajakan barang-barangnya, dan bau asap dupa atau suara syahdu orang-orang yang menyanyikan kidung-kidung pujaan -- semua itu membuat aku lupa akan keletihanku. Suasana yang agak liar ini memang berbeda benar dengan suasana Kirene yang sopan dan tertib. Namun, lebih hidup. Tiba-tiba ada kegaduhan yang tak biasa. Para serdadu Roma menyeruak massa. "Ah, lagi-lagi pawai laskar-laskar Romawi untuk mengingatkan siapa yang berkuasa di negeri ini," pikirku. Akan tetapi tidak. Di baris paling depan, ada seorang serdadu yang memegang panji bertulis: "Yesus, orang Nazaret, raja orang Yahudi." Aku memang belum pernah berjumpa dengan-Nya. Akan tetapi, nama "Yesus", siapa yang tidak mengenal-Nya? Dia adalah tokoh paling kontroversial. Yang tidak dapat kumengerti, mengapa serdadu Romawi mengarak panji seperti itu. Karena itu, aku mendekat untuk melihat lebih dekat. Di tengah pagar betis laskar-laskar Roma itu, tiga orang melangkah pelan memanggul salib. "Penjahat-penjahat besar," pikirku. Namun, apa hubungannya dengan panji itu? Kemudian aku semakin mengerti. Riuh rendah massa rakyat menyebut-nyebut nama Yesus sambil mencemooh-Nya. Tidak kurang pula yang meludahi-Nya. Akan tetapi, yang manakah Yesus di antara ketiga orang itu? Aku Simon dari Kirene. Aku semakin mendekat. Lalu aku tahu dengan pasti yang mana Yesus. Dia paling kecil, hampir tidak berotot. Rambut panjang-Nya terurai, lekat di sana-sini oleh darah kering yang berasal dari duri-duri yang teranyam di kepala-Nya. Sekujur tubuh-Nya biru lebam. Langkah-Nya tertatih-tatih. Amat letih. Akan tetapi mata-Nya -- meski merah sebab kurang tidur -- namun tetap tajam menusuk setiap kali menatap. Anehnya, juga begitu lembut menyejukkan. Aku tak dapat lepas memandang mata-Nya itu. Penuh wibawa, tetapi juga begitu menenangkan dan kebapakan. Lalu Dia roboh. Tubuh-Nya yang kecil dan nyaris hancur itu tidak kuat lagi menahan bobot salib di pundak-Nya. Massa berteriak kesenangan bagai binatang liar yang haus darah. Cemeti melayang menyayat punggung-Nya. Darah menyembur. Dan Dia pun bangkit lagi pelan-pelan. Keletihan. Tetapi mata-Nya itu, oi, mata-Nya. Lalu Dia berjalan beberapa langkah. Namun, roboh lagi. Arak-arakan berhenti. Massa semakin buas. Cemeti melayang berulang-ulang. Darah menyembur. Namun, Dia tak mampu bangun kembali. Aku Simon dari Kirene. Entah mengapa, aku tidak terkesan benar oleh semua itu. Kecuali oleh tatapan mata-Nya. Mata-Nya itu, oi, mata-Nya. content_zh:
我是来自古利内的西门。我的名字表明我住在非洲大陆。尽管如此，我的皮肤并不黑，嘴唇也不厚。尽管我的家族已经在昔兰尼生活了几代人，昔兰尼是昔兰尼加的首府，这是一座位于北非的希腊城市，以其繁荣和哲学家而闻名，但我的肤色并不白。我是古利奈的西门。

我从心底里是一个地道的犹太人。从小到大，我毫无例外地遵守所有宗教律法，尽管由于在讲希腊语的社区长大，我已经不再精通阿拉姆语。我是古利奈人西门。我不想谈论我自己。也不想讲述我所有的生活经历。我只想讲述我那一次的经历。

这段经历后来改变了我的人生轨迹。如果您也经历过，那么也会改变您的人生轨迹。那天是星期五。那天早上我刚抵达耶路撒冷。我长途跋涉的目的就是为了庆祝逾越节。我每年都这样做。看到熙熙攘攘的人群挤满了这座城市，我一点也不感到惊讶。

尽管很累，但在酒店放下行李并洗漱完毕后，我还是出门散步，享受这座沉浸在节日气氛中的城市的喧嚣。

到处跑来跑去的孩子们尖叫声，叫卖的小贩们劝诱甚至有时强迫的吆喝声，还有熏香的味道或人们吟唱赞美诗的悠扬声音——这一切都让我忘记了疲惫。这种略显喧闹的氛围与古利奈文雅有序的氛围截然不同，但却更有活力。

突然间，出现了一阵不寻常的喧哗。罗马士兵挤过人群。“唉，又是罗马士兵的游行，用来提醒人们谁才是这个国家的统治者。”我想。但是不是。在最前面一排，有一名士兵拿着一面旗帜，上面写着：“拿撒勒人耶稣，犹太人的王。” 我确实从未见过祂。

但是，“耶稣”这个名字，谁不认识他呢？他是最具争议的人物。我不明白的是，为什么罗马士兵要举着这样的旗帜游行。因此，我走近仔细观察。在罗马士兵的方阵中间，有三个人背着十字架缓缓前行。“大坏蛋，”我想。不过，这和那面旗帜有什么关系？

然后我渐渐明白了。人群喧嚣着，一边喊着耶稣的名字，一边嘲笑祂。还有不少人向祂吐唾沫。但是，这三个人当中哪一个是耶稣呢？我是古利奈人西门。我走得越来越近。然后我确切地知道谁是耶稣。他是三人中个子最小的，几乎没有肌肉。

祂的长发散乱，这里那里都沾满了干涸的血迹，这些血迹来自祂头上戴着的荆棘冠。祂的全身都瘀青了。祂的步伐蹒跚。祂非常疲惫。但是祂的眼睛——尽管因为睡眠不足而发红——但每次注视时仍然锐利如刀。奇怪的是，他的眼神也如此温柔、令人舒心。我无法移开视线，不去看祂的眼睛。

充满威严，但也非常平和和慈父般。然后祂倒下了。祂瘦小而几乎破碎的身体再也承受不住肩上十字架的重量。人群像嗜血的野兽一样欢呼雀跃。鞭子抽打着祂的背。鲜血喷涌而出。祂又慢慢地站了起来。祂疲惫不堪。但是祂的眼睛，哎呀，祂的眼睛。

然后他走了几步。然而，祂又倒下了。游行队伍停了下来。人群变得越来越凶狠。鞭子一次又一次地挥舞着。鲜血喷涌而出。然而，祂再也无法站起来了。我是古利奈人西门。不知为何，这一切并没有真正触动我。除了祂的眼神。祂的眼睛，哎呀，祂的眼睛。

因此，当一名士兵突然拉我时，我好像失去了知觉。然后把十字架放在我身上。

title: Kasih Tuhan Tiada Taranya
summary_zh: p style="margin-bottom:1em; ">作者：Romauli br Marpaung Shalom，我叫 Romauli br Marpaung。
title_zh: 上帝的爱是无与伦比的
content: p style="margin-bottom:1em;">Oleh: Romauli br Marpaung Shalom, Nama saya Romauli br Marpaung. Saat ini, saya berusia 23 tahun. Saya berasal dari keluarga Kristen. Saya anak pertama dari lima bersaudara. Keluarga saya, dahulunya, bukan keluarga yang harmonis. Orang tua saya sering bertengkar. Namun, saat kelas IV SD, bapak saya bertobat sungguh-sungguh dan menyerahkan dirinya untuk diperlengkapi di Sekolah Alkitab Purbasari Pematang Siantar. Setelah selesai sekolah, beliau akhirnya diangkat menjadi seorang Pendeta, dan saya mulai pelayanan sejak kelas V SD di Gereja Kemuliaan Sion sebagai pemain musik tunggal. Pada 2013, saat saya lulus SMA, saya berharap bisa kuliah di Universitas Sumatera Utara (USU) Medan. Namun, saat mengikuti SBMPTN, saya gagal karena tidak lulus seleksi. Akhirnya, bapak saya mengusulkan supaya saya kuliah di Solo karena dia punya rekan pendeta yang anaknya kuliah di Solo juga. Saya mengikuti keinginan bapak saya karena beliau rindu saya bisa menjadi seorang hamba Tuhan. Akhirnya, saya kuliah di STT Berita Hidup, Solo, dan mengikuti semua kegiatan, aturan yang ada di kampus tersebut. Saya dibaptis saat duduk di bangku SMA kelas XI. Awalnya, saya kuliah di Berita Hidup karena orang tua dan pelarian, tetapi pada akhirnya saya bertobat dan percaya sungguh-sungguh kepada Tuhan Yesus saat kuliah semester 2. Pelayanan-pelayanan yang Tuhan percayakan kepada saya itu tidak mudah. Ada banyak masalah yang saya hadapi, baik itu dari asrama, tempat pelayanan, maupun kampus. Kalau bukan karena kekuatan Tuhan, mungkin saya tidak mampu. Namun, Tuhan Yesus baik, Dia memberi pertolongan saat saya benar-benar tidak mampu menjalaninya. Saya pelayanan di Gereja Bethel Tabernakel, Karanganyar. Saya mulai melayani di sana sejak Agustus 2014 sampai saat ini. Saya dipercaya untuk melayani di beberapa bagian, seperti melayani anak-anak sekolah minggu, pemuda/remaja, jemaat dewasa, maupun yang sudah lanjut usia. Selain itu, saya juga ambil bagian dalam musik, yaitu melatih anak-anak sekolah minggu belajar musik. Selain itu, saya juga diberi kesempatan oleh pendeta saya untuk membuka Bimbingan Belajar di Bibis Luhur Solo. Sewaktu kuliah, saya ditempatkan praktik tahunan di Gereja Kristus Rahmani Indonesia (GKRI), Jimbaran Bali. Tantangan yang saya hadapi adalah saya melayani orang-orang Kristen yang sudah berkeluarga, tetapi belum terikat dalam pernikahan. Saya juga membantu mengajar di PAUD Shinam, Jimbaran, milik gereja tersebut. Saya bersyukur untuk semua pelayanan yang telah dipercayakan gereja kepada saya. Saya bisa menjalani semua ini dengan pertolongan Tuhan. Yang saya rindukan dalam pelayanan adalah saya bisa memberikan yang terbaik untuk Tuhan dan gereja, menjadi berkat bagi banyak orang, dan tetap setia terhadap panggilan Tuhan. Saya juga rindu suatu saat saya bisa membuka pelayanan sendiri. Saya tahu itu tidak mudah, tetapi saya percaya kuasa pertolongan Tuhan nyata bagi saya. Kiranya kesaksian ini bisa menjadi berkat bagi semua orang, dan saya rindu kita tetap percaya bahwa segala sesuatu yang kita lakukan untuk Tuhan tidak akan kembali dengan sia-sia, melainkan Dia akan memberkati kita senantiasa (Kolose 3:23). Mulailah mengatakan bahwa pelayanan itu adalah sebuah kehormatan, bukan beban. Tuhan Yesus memberkati. "Dan, Maria berkata, "Sesungguhnya, aku ini hamba Tuhan. Terjadilah padaku seperti yang engkau katakan itu." Kemudian, malaikat itu pergi meninggalkannya."(Lukas 1:38, AYT)

p style="margin-bottom:1em;">作者：Romauli br Marpaung Shalom，我叫 Romauli br Marpaung。我今年 23 岁。我来自一个基督徒家庭。我是五个兄弟姐妹中的老大。我的家庭以前并不和谐。我的父母经常吵架。

然而，当我上小学四年级时，我父亲真心悔改，并前往位于Pematang Siantar的Purbasari圣经学校接受装备。毕业后，他最终被任命为牧师，而我从小学五年级开始就在锡安荣耀教会担任独奏乐手。

2013 年，当我高中毕业时，我希望能在棉兰的北苏门答腊大学 (USU) 上大学。然而，在参加全国统一高考（SBMPTN）时，我因为没有通过选拔而落榜了。最后，我父亲建议我去梭罗上大学，因为他有一位牧师朋友，他的孩子也在梭罗上大学。我听从了父亲的意愿，因为他希望我能成为神的仆人。

最后，我在梭罗的生命福音神学院（STT Berita Hidup）上学，并参加了该校的所有活动，遵守了该校的所有规定。我在读高一的时候受洗。起初，我因为父母和逃避现实的原因而就读于生命信息神学院，但最终我在第二学期时悔改并真心信靠主耶稣。

神托付给我的服侍并不容易。我面临着很多问题，无论是来自宿舍、事工场所还是校园。如果不是因为上帝的力量，我可能无法做到。然而，主耶稣是良善的，当我已经实在无法承受时，祂会伸出援手。我在卡朗亚尔的伯特利会幕教会（Gereja Bethel Tabernakel）服侍。

我从 2014 年 8 月开始在那里服侍，至今仍在继续。我受托在几个部门服侍，例如服侍主日学儿童、青年/青少年、成年会众以及老年人。此外，我还参与音乐方面的工作，即指导主日学儿童学习音乐。

此外，我的牧师还给了我机会，在梭罗的Bibis Luhur开设学习辅导班。在大学期间，我被安排在巴厘岛金巴兰的印度尼西亚基督慈悲教会（GKRI）进行年度实习。我面临的挑战是我要服侍那些已经有家庭但尚未缔结婚姻的基督徒。

我还协助在属于该教会的金巴兰 Shinam 幼儿教育中心（PAUD Shinam）进行教学。我感谢教会将所有这些事工托付给我。在神的帮助下，我能够做到这一切。我在侍奉中渴望的是，我能够为上帝和教会尽我所能，成为许多人的祝福，并始终忠于上帝的呼召。

我也希望有一天我能自己开办一间教会。我知道这并不容易，但我相信上帝的帮助对我来说是真实的。愿这个见证能成为所有人的祝福，我希望我们能继续相信，我们为神所做的一切都不会徒劳无功，祂必会永远赐福于我们（歌罗西书 3:23）。

开始说服自己，服侍是一种荣誉，而不是一种负担。愿主耶稣赐福。 “马利亚说：‘我是主的使女。愿照你的话成就在我身上。” 天使就离开她去了。”（路加福音 1:38，AYT）

content: Antes de escribir la biografía de Jorge Bergoglio, que llamó El gran Reformador, Austen Ivereigh ya era un experto en la historia de la Iglesia argentina. “Mi tesis de doctorado [en Oxford], que terminé en el 92, fue sobre catolicismo y política en la Argentina”. Y hay más: “Debo mi fe a la Iglesia Argentina, leyendo artículos de monseñor (Gustavo) Franceschi, volví a la fe”, dice. Ese conocimiento de nuestro país y de su fe mayoritaria representó una ventaja a la hora de escribir sobre Bergoglio, ya que cada etapa de la trayectoria del futuro Papa está debidamente contextualizada en la época que atravesaba el país. Desde aquel marzo de 2013, cuando la novedad de un pontífice argentino y jesuita impactó al mundo entero, Ivereihg siempre pensó que vendría cuando Francisco visitara la Argentina, viaje que finalmente no se concretó. “Ahora vengo con León”, comenta. En efecto, este escritor, historiador, periodista y analista de asuntos religiosos y políticos estará en nuestro país contemporáneamente con la visita del papa León XIV, invitado por la Universidad del Salvador (USAL), donde dictó, el pasado viernes 6, una clase magistral sobre “El giro latinoamericano Francisco-León: la Iglesia misionera sinodal y el cambio de época”. Ivereigh también es co-autor de Let Us Dream (Soñemos Juntos, 2020), un libro escrito en colaboración con Francisco. Su trabajo más reciente es First Belong to God: On Retreat with Pope Francis (Lo primero es pertenecer a Dios: Un retiro con el Papa Francisco, 2024), basado en los escritos y charlas de Bergoglio como director espiritual de un retiro ignaciano de 8 días. De 2004 a 2006, Ivereigh fue colaborador del entonces arzobispo de Westminster, cardenal Cormac Murphy-O’Connor, uno de los más activos promotores de la candidatura de Jorge Mario Bergoglio al papado. Ivereigh considera que el papado de Francisco inició un giro latinoamericano hacia una iglesia misionera y sinodal, cuyo primer paso fue la exhortación apostólica Evangelii Gaudium (noviembre de 2013), sobre “el anuncio del Evangelio en el mundo actual”, con la cual, dice, “Francisco inaugura una hoja de ruta de su Papado que también es la del pontificado de León”. Pero esa hoja de ruta tenía una génesis anterior: el ya famoso documento de Aparecida, la V Conferencia General del Episcopado Latinoamericano y del Caribe (Celam), redactado por Bergoglio. De esta manera, “América Latina pasó a ser la iglesia fuente”, señala, porque “siempre hay una parte de la Iglesia de la cual brota un dinamismo teológico”. Antes, ese rol lo cumplía Europa, pero a partir del Concilio Vaticano II eso cambia porque es en América Latina donde mejor se lo pone en práctica. Aclara que “fuente” no quiere decir centro; de hecho, “Francisco quería una Iglesia multipolar”. — ¿Hasta qué punto Aparecida refleja a Bergoglio como individualidad y hasta dónde es la Iglesia latinoamericana, que usted define como “fuente”? — El proceso de preparación de esa conferencia general, fue muy sinodal, de mucha consulta, y el papel de Bergoglio en esa conferencia general es muy conocido. Creo que influyó la recepción del Concilio Vaticano II en el Río de La Plata, que tuvo un matiz distinto al resto de América Latina. Tal vez, cuando llegó a Aparecida esa visión sobre la religiosidad popular estaba ya madura. Es decir, una teología de espiritualidad latinoamericana, distinta a anteriores teologías latinoamericanas. Bergoglio tenía muchas cosas que eran de él. Pero también llevaba en su forma de ser y de pensar muchos aportes de la iglesia argentina, la influencia de Lucio Gera y de Rafael Tello y toda esa tradición. — ¿Cómo vio el impacto de su papado en la Argentina? — Creo que una de las razones por las que no vino, sobre todo al principio, fue que tenía horror del triunfalismo. Y sabía que tal vez los argentinos tenían —todos los países lo tienen— una cierta tentación de decir: “El Papa es argentino”. title_zh: Calendar creștin ortodox joi, 22 octombrie 2026. Rugăciunea către Sfinźii șapte tineri din Efes, rstită pentru liniște sufletească și somn odihnitor
content: Calendarul creștin ortodox pentru joi, 22 octombrie 2026, îi pomenește pe Sfinții șapte tineri din Efes, cunoscuți și sub numele de „cei șapte adormiți”. Aceștia sunt sărbătoriți de Biserica Ortodoxă de două ori pe an, pe 22 octombrie și pe 4 august. Povestea lor este legată de o peșteră din Muntele Ohlonului, unde, potrivit tradiției creștine, au dormit vreme de mai multe sute de ani. Credincioșii se pot ruga către aceștia pentru liniște sufletească și odihnă. Cine sunt Sfinții șapte tineri din Efes Sfinții șapte tineri din Efes sunt Maximilian, Exacustodian, Iamvlih, Martinian, Dionisie, Ioan și Constantin. Potrivit tradiției creștine, aceștia au trăit în vremea împăratului Deciu, când creștinii erau persecutați pentru credința lor. Pentru a se adăposti de prigoană, cei șapte tineri s-au retras într-o peșteră din Muntele Ohlonului, unde au adormit pentru mai multe sute de ani. Tot joi, 22 octombrie, Biserica Ortodoxă îl pomenește și pe Sfântul Averchie, episcopul cetății Ierapole din Frigia. În aceeași zi mai sunt pomeniți Sfântul Kukșa din Odesa, Sfântul Mucenic Alexandru episcopul, Mucenicul Iraclie, Anna, Elisaveta, Teodota și Glicheria, Sfântul Mucenic Zaharia, Sfântul Ruf și Cuviosul Lot. Rugăciunea către Sfinții șapte tineri din Efes, pentru liniște sufletească și odihnă Credincioșii care se confruntă cu griji și lipsa somnului pot rosti rugăciunea către Sfinții șapte tineri din Efes, cerând ajutor pentru dobândirea păcii sufletești. „Sfinților 7 tineri din Efes, care bine v-ați nevoit și cununa Împăratului Hristos ați dobândit, ne rugăm vouă, ca unii care multă îndrăzneală înaintea Domnului ați câștigat. Sfinților Maximilian, Exacustodian, Iamvlih, Martinian, Dionisie, Ioan şi Constantin, izbăviți-ne de lipsa somnului și puținătatea sufletului. Citește și: Carmen Harra, mesaj pentru populație! Ce s-ar putea întâmpla în 2027: “Nimeni nu spune adevărul!” Citește si: Andreea Pirui a fost prinsă de oamenii legii! Unde a fost găsită Voi, care în vremea împăratului Deciu, prigonitorul, ați fost pregătiți să luați cununa muceniciei, mărturisind dreapta credință și împotrivindu-vă tiranului celui fără de omenie, însă, din rânduială dumnezeiască, peștera în care v-ați adăpostit nu v-a fost vouă mormânt, ci s-a făcut vouă sân al lui Avraam, în care ați dormit somn adânc mai multe sute de ani şi, ca nişte prunci ce se încălzesc la sânul maicii lor, nu ați suferit nicio stricăciune. Iar în vremea binecredinciosului împărat Teodosie, din încredințarea Mântuitorului și pentru adeverirea Învierii celei de obște, v-ați trezit și v-ați arătat oamenilor, dând mărturie despre puterea lui Dumnezeu, apoi ați adormit cu adevărat întru odihna cea veșnică. O, preaslăvită minune, încât pretutindeni oamenii o au cunoscut. Deci, și acum, când gânduri negre vin asupra noastră, văzând cum slăbim cu duhul și cum ne descurajăm din lipsa somnului, acestea ne rod și ne macină sufletește, ca un vierme neadormit. Grijile cele apăsătoare, ca niște ulii la pradă, ne covârșesc și nu mai știm ce sunt pacea și odihna încrederii în Dumnezeu. Știm că toate acestea pentru păcatele noastre sunt. Știm că, pentru puțina noastră iubire de Dumnezeu și de aproapele, în astfel de mâhniri se afundă sufletul nostru. Cu pocăință ne rugăm și cerem ajutorul vostru, Sfinților din Efes, somn binecuvântat și mângâietor, spre pacea sufletului și odihna cea trupească, dăruiți-ne. Izbăviți-ne din gândurile cele rele, iar cu cele bune ne insuflați. Scoateți-ne din grijile cele multe care ne macină și de singură grija mântuirii învățați-ne să ne ținem. Așadar, Sfinților ai lui Dumnezeu, prin ajutorul vostru, luminare și împăcare întru Hristos să găsim și cerul să îl dobândim. Amin.”

title: Félix Lungu : É muito difícil ser cristão em países fundamentais
summary: É a maior comunidade religiosa, mas também a mais perseguida do mundo. Os cristãos são notícia quase diariamente por serem alvo de ataques ou assassínios; ou por as suas instalações e símbolos terem s
summary_zh: É a maior comunidade religiosa, mas também a mais perseguida do mundo. Os cristãos são notícia quase diariamente por serem alvo de ataques ou assassínios ； ou por as suas instalações e símbolos terem s
title_zh: Félix Lungu ： É muito difícil ser cristão em países fundamentais
content: É a maior comunidade religiosa, mas também a mais perseguida do mundo. Os cristãos são notícia quase diariamente por serem alvo de ataques ou assassínios; ou por as suas instalações e símbolos terem sido danificados. Só em setembro, o Observatory on Intolerance and Discrimination against Christians dá conta de 30 casos na Europa, entre atos de vandalismo a igrejas, cemitérios, ataques a sacerdotes - um foi assassinado - ou mesmo a discriminação profissional por se ser cristão. Se a Nigéria é considerada o país mais perigoso para os católicos, o México é o inferno para padres, pois é aí que mais são assassinados. O Nascer do SOL entrevista Félix Lungu, um romeno a viver em Portugal há 31 anos, porta-voz, em Portugal, da fundação Ajuda à Igreja que Sofre (AIS). Esta organização faz relatórios sobre a liberdade religiosa no mundo, e tenta explicar onde as religiões são mais perseguidas e quais os desafios que enfrentam, com especial ênfase na Igreja Católica. Félix Langu, à semelhança dos seus chefes - a organização tem sede na Alemanha -, procura não alimentar divisões, mas é impossível fugir a factos: no Paquistão, só muito recentemente é que os empresários do lixo deixaram de recrutar obrigatoriamente cristãos; não faltam países fundamentalistas onde meninas de 10 anos são violadas e obrigadas a casar, ‘adquirindo’ automaticamente a religião islâmica; e são ainda muitas as nações onde os católicos não podem desempenhar cargos na função pública. O Vaticano calcula que, anualmente, são mortos cerca de cinco mil cristãos, mas a liberdade religiosa afeta também os muçulmanos moderados, que são alvo da ira dos fundamentalistas, acabando muitos deles assassinados. Qual o papel da Fundação Ajuda à Igreja que Sofre? A Ajuda à Igreja que Sofre, fundação Pontifícia, é uma organização que tem quase 80 anos e foi criada na Alemanha. Nasceu no final da Segunda Guerra Mundial para ajudar os refugiados alemães que se deslocavam pela Europa. Depois, pouco a pouco, ajudou cristãos dos países do Leste, por causa do comunismo, do ateísmo, de toda essa situação. Ou seja, não somos como a Cáritas, ou outras ONGs, no sentido de dar ajuda social, ou educação, ou saúde. Também chegamos a estas áreas, o foco, contudo, é a ajuda pastoral, ajudar a Igreja, ajudar sacerdotes, construir igrejas, formação de seminaristas, ajudar nas missões os missionários, com carros, com rádios, televisões, bíblias, o que é necessário para fazer a evangelização. Basicamente é isso e estamos em 24 países. A sede é na Alemanha, onde se faz a gestão de tudo isso. E nos outros 24 secretariados fazemos a angariação de fundos. Para fazer a angariação de fundos é preciso saber por que se pede dinheiro, por que se pede esta ajuda. Temos três pilares, digamos assim, da nossa missão: informar, rezar e ajudar. Informar é tentar dizer qual é a situação no mundo, sobretudo onde há carências, que tipo de carências, sempre com foco nesta dimensão pastoral ou de evangelização. Nos últimos anos, a Ajuda à Igreja que Sofre dedica-se ao estudo ou análise da situação da liberdade religiosa no mundo. Porque se nós somos uma organização da Igreja, e se temos parceiros em todo o mundo, em 186 países, é importante saber onde há carências, que tipo de carências são. E temos percebido que, por exemplo, no Médio Oriente, junto com as carências materiais, falta de escola, de saúde, da alimentação, há também esta dimensão da perseguição. Falta algo que valorizamos muito, que é a questão da liberdade religiosa, dos direitos, que estão valorizados no ocidente. O que fazem nesses países onde os cristão são perseguidos? Na Arábia Saudita, por exemplo, não há hipótese de haver uma igreja? Não, na Arábia Saudita não temos uma presença. A única presença nesses países é através da representação consular. É na capela de uma embaixada, por exemplo, de França ou de Itália, que se pode celebrar a missa, porque não há possibilidade de ter uma igreja na Arábia Saudita. Considerado o país do profeta, terra sagrada

title: The Cross : The Suffering To Which ALL Christians Are Called
summary: By Bradlee Dean October 21, 2026 “For unto you it is given on behalf of Christ, not only to believe in Him, but also to suffer for His sake…”-Philippians 1:29 When it comes to suffering, there is not
summary_zh: 2026年10月21日，布拉德利·迪恩（ Bradlee Dean ）写道： “因为这是代表基督给你的，不仅要相信他，而且要为他而受苦……” --腓立比书1:29说到受苦，没有
title_zh: 十字架：所有基督徒被称为的苦难
content: By Bradlee Dean October 21, 2026 “For unto you it is given on behalf of Christ, not only to believe in Him, but also to suffer for His sake…”-Philippians 1:29 When it comes to suffering, there is not a genuine Christian who is not appointed to it. Why? For His sake. “For we preach not ourselves, but Christ Jesus the Lord; and ourselves your servants for Jesus’ sake. For God, who commanded the light to shine out of darkness, hath shined in our hearts, to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ. But we have this treasure in earthen vessels, that the excellency of the power may be of God, and not of us. We are troubled on every side, yet not distressed; we are perplexed, but not in despair; Persecuted, but not forsaken; cast down, but not destroyed; Always bearing about in the body the dying of the Lord Jesus, that the life also of Jesus might be made manifest in our body. For we which live are always delivered unto death for Jesus’ sake, that the life also of Jesus might be made manifest in our mortal flesh. So then death worketh in us, but life in you. We having the same spirit of faith, according as it is written, I believed, and therefore have I spoken; we also believe, and therefore speak; Knowing that he which raised up the Lord Jesus shall raise up us also by Jesus, and shall present us with you. For all things are for your sakes, that the abundant grace might through the thanksgiving of many redound to the glory of God.” –2 Corinthians 4:5-15 I also realize that no one spoke of, or endured, suffering more than Christ, though ours are light in comparison (Isaiah 53), who told us before His ascension that as the Father sent Him, so He would send us (John 20:21). I have personally suffered, including fellowship with His sufferings, afflictions, trials, and testings, so that I might learn and grow from the lessons the Lord gives in the process (Psalm 119:71). Oftentimes we think we are in control of our own world; we may even deceive ourselves into believing we are trusting the Lord and are being led by His Spirit (Romans 8:14) when we are not, only to find that in the end we were all the while limiting Him through our means of control. For example, we can pray, Lord, increase our faith, or, Lord, oh, that I would grow in grace more so I might be just like you, and then, when He brings us through the process to learn the lessons, we lose control, and there it is: we find out who it is that we really are, and who it is that we really trust (John 3:6). We have heard some say that the Lord will never give us more than we can handle, and I have to say, this is not true whatsoever, because in many cases He brings us to the place of more than we can handle to show us what we cannot handle, to show us what it is that He can handle, and this with ease. This is done so that we trust not in ourselves (2 Corinthians 1: 5-10). In other words, our extremity is the Lord’s opportunity. You see, the root of fear is control, and throughout our lives we are taught to control every aspect of our lives so that we do not have to trust in the Lord (avoid suffering) that we may grow, though we claim that we are doing so. Then, when we lose that control, we have to trust the Lord in ways that we never have before, this where we suffer through our unbelief (though we hold to His Word) until we transition (by the Holy Ghost – Titus 3:5) into what it is that He means for us to be, and to see outside of our own limited controls in order to bring us into a larger place (Psalm 4:1). Isaiah 55:8-9 says, “For my thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways, saith the LORD. For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways, and my thoughts than your thoughts.” In conclusion: Through suffering, the Lord introduces us to His workings, so that we might see His faithfulness, to see His wonderful works which are His righteous operations in and through Christ, as we are confo
content_zh:
2026年10月21日 布莱德利·迪恩 “为了你们,不仅为了信仰基督,而且为了他而受苦受难。” 关于受苦,没有一个真正的基督徒没有被任命。 为什么? 为他故. " 我们不是为自己而传教,而是为主而传教;我们是你们的仆人;

因为上帝命令光从黑暗中闪出,已经照亮了我们的心,在耶稣基督面前赋予了上帝的荣耀知识之光. 但我们有这个宝藏在地上, 权力的卓越可能来自上帝,而不是我们。 我们每边都忧心忡忡,却不忧愁;我们感到困惑,但不是绝望;我们受到迫害,但不是被遗弃;

我们有着同样的信仰精神,按照它所写的,我相信,因此我说过话;我们也相信,因而也说出话来;我们知道,复活主耶稣的人,也要由耶稣来养育我们,并将我们与你一同呈现.

万事都是为你着想的,丰厚的恩典,可以通过许多为上帝所荣耀而赞颂的恩惠来达到。” ——2 科林斯人4:5-15 我也意识到,没有人会说出或忍受比基督更痛苦的事,尽管我们的比喻是轻的(以赛亚53),在他升天之前,他告诉我们,正如父亲派遣他那样,他将派遣我们(约翰20:21)。

我个人遭受了痛苦,包括同他的痛苦、苦难、考验和试验的友谊,以便我能够从上帝在这一过程中提供的经验教训(第119:71段)中吸取并成长。 我们常常认为我们控制着自己的世界;

我们甚至可以欺骗自己,使我们相信我们信任主,并且正被他的精神所引导,而我们不是那样的,我们只是发现,我们最终通过我们的控制而限制他。

例如,我们可以祈祷,主,增加我们的信仰,或者,主, 哦,我将会在恩典中成长得更多,这样我或许就和你一样,然后,当他带我们走进吸取教训的过程时,我们失去控制,这就是:我们发现我们真正是谁,我们真正信任谁(John 3:6)。

我们听到有人说,上帝永远不会给我们 超过我们所能处理, 我必须说,这不是真的,因为在许多情况下, 他带我们到我们无法处理的地方 向我们展示我们无法处理的事 向我们展示他能处理的事 以及轻松处理的事 这样做是为了让我们不信任自己(2个哥林多1:5-10).

换句话说,我们的极限是上帝的机会。 你看,恐惧的根源是控制,在我们一生中,我们被教导要控制我们生活的方方面面,这样我们不必相信主(避免痛苦),以便我们成长,尽管我们声称我们这样做了.

然后,当我们失去这种控制时,我们必须以我们以前从未有过的方式信任上帝,这是我们通过不信而受苦的地方(尽管我们坚持他的话),直到我们(由圣灵-提图斯3:5)过渡到他对我们意味着什么,并且看到我们自己有限的控制之外,以便把我们带入更大的地方(Psalm 4:1).

以赛亚55:8-9说:"耶和华说,我的想法不是你们的,你们的道路也不是我的。

因为天比地高,我的道路也比地高;我的思想也比地高。” 最后:主通过苦难向我们介绍他的工作,以便我们看见他的忠诚,看到他的出色的作品,这是他在基督中和通过基督的正义行动,就像我们聚集在一起一样。

title: De la pesadilla de Gaza al sueño de Fatma : cómo podemos seguir creyendo en la humanidad en medio del horror
summary: “I have a dream”, decía Martin Luther King en 1963, cuando agitaba las conciencias desde las escalinatas del monumento a Lincoln en Washington, en uno de los discursos más emblemáticos de la historia.
summary_zh: “我有一个梦想” ， decía Martin Luther King en 1963, cuando agitaba las conciencias desde las escalinatas del monumento a Lincoln en Washington, en uno de los discursos más emblemáticos de la historia。
title_zh: De la pesadilla de Gaza al sueño de Fatma: cómo podemos seguir creyendo en la humanidad en medio del horror
content: “I have a dream”, decía Martin Luther King en 1963, cuando agitaba las conciencias desde las escalinatas del monumento a Lincoln en Washington, en uno de los discursos más emblemáticos de la historia. Hoy, sin embargo, sólo siento ganas de decir: I have a nightmare. O mejor dicho: We have a nightmare, porque la pesadilla no sólo afecta a los palestinos, sino a todos nosotros, a cualquiera que cree que la “justicia” no es una palabra vacía. La vida de los palestinos es una pesadilla interminable. En Gaza oyes el ruido de los aviones, sientes el miedo de los bombardeos, el acecho de los drones –cada vez más traicioneros y sofisticados– que te siguen, te espían, te ensordecen y disparan. La vida cotidiana consiste en sobrevivir en tiendas de campaña desgarradas por el viento y llenas de barro. Compartir un baño con tanta gente que usarlo se vuelve imposible. Volver a una casa medio destruida por las bombas con el riesgo de que el techo se derrumbe y mate a tu familia. Afrontar el rigor del invierno –ya es el tercero desde que comenzó el genocidio–, sin ni siquiera unos libros que poder quemar para mantener a tus seres queridos, al menos a los niños y ancianos, en un lugar cálido y seguro. Sólo tiendas, frías en invierno, sofocantes en los tórridos veranos. Cuántos muertos, desplazados, huérfanos, heridos, mutilados… Y los que aún no han sucumbido al asedio total que impera desde hace más de dos años están condenados a sufrir hambre y sed, a no tener derecho a una asistencia sanitaria y a una supervivencia digna. En Cisjordania y en Jerusalén Este, los palestinos viven con el terror de despertarse en plena noche con un soldado que los apunta con un fusil a la cara, que destruye sus casas, que los amenaza, los humilla delante de sus hijos o se los lleva consigo, con sus pijamas manchados de pipí porque se han orinado encima de miedo. Mientras tanto, los colonos están cada vez más furiosos: los ataques a los pueblos, comunidades rurales, tierras, coches, ganado, están a la orden del día. Incluso en las cárceles hay casos documentados en los que se ha autorizado a periodistas y civiles israelíes a presenciar –e incluso a grabar con sus teléfonos móviles– los abusos infligidos a prisioneros palestinos, a quienes deberíamos llamar “rehenes”, dada la falta de garantías mínimas legales que caracteriza las detenciones israelíes en el territorio palestino ocupado. Esta fragmentación territorial, legal y política es la institucionalización de la excepción; es la transformación de la precariedad en condiciones permanentes; es un sistema en el que la ocupación militar y la colonización ya no son sucesos aislados, sino un régimen consolidado en el que el control no sólo se ejerce con las armas sino también mediante la planificación urbanística, la burocracia, la segmentación administrativa, con la creación de categorías jurídicas diferenciadas para personas que viven en el mismo espacio pero no bajo los mismos derechos. Y después de décadas, la violencia de esta época nos indica que hemos llegado a la fase final: la del genocidio, la de la guerra de Israel contra un pueblo que hasta ahora ha resistido como ha podido. La mujer que amasa el pan bajo los drones, el maestro que sigue enseñando bajo las tiendas, la familia que planta un limonero donde el día antes había una casa, las parejas que siguen casándose y –también en el infierno de Gaza– trayendo hijos al mundo. Es ahí donde la esperanza se vuelve radical: el sueño de un mundo que persiste y que, si nos esforzamos, puede mejorar. Este sueño es el corazón palpitante de la resistencia palestina En los últimos dos años las cosas han ido todavía a peor: el terror se ha vuelto omnipresente, cotidiano. Se trata de una pesadilla que ha alcanzado dimensiones delirantes a los ojos del mundo. Pero es cuando todo se derrumba a nuestro alrededor, entre el horror y la esperanza, que resulta indispensable comenzar a soñar. title_zh: 对话与福传：必须二选其一吗？
content: Dans un monde traversé par les tensions religieuses, les replis identitaires et les conflits, le dialogue interreligieux apparaît plus que jamais nécessaire. La rencontre, l’écoute, la fraternité et la recherche de la paix sont des exigences profondément évangéliques. Mais une question demeure : le dialogue suffit-il à accomplir la mission que Jésus a confié à l’Église ? La fraternité entre croyants de différentes religions peut-elle tenir lieu, voire remplacer aujourd’hui, l’annonce de Jésus-Christ et la proposition de la foi ? La question mérite d’être posée sans caricaturer les différentes sensibilités missionnaires. D’un côté, l’Église ne peut ignorer les contextes culturels, politiques ou religieux dans lesquels elle est appelée à vivre et témoigner : dans certains pays, notamment là où les chrétiens sont très minoritaires et ne jouissent pas d’une pleine liberté religieuse, la présence fraternelle, le service et le témoignage de vie constituent des modalités essentielles de sa mission. 在一个充斥着宗教紧张、身份认同退缩和冲突的世界中，宗教间对话比以往任何时候都显得更加必要。相遇、倾听、博爱和寻求和平是福音的深刻要求。但一个问题依然存在：对话是否足以完成耶稣赋予教会的使命？

在当今时代，不同宗教信仰者之间的兄弟情谊能否取代，甚至替代对耶稣基督的宣扬和对信仰的提倡？这个问题值得提出，但同时不应夸大不同的传教敏感性。

content: On le surnomme l’ »Apôtre du Pérou ». Saint Toribio de Mogrovejo (1538-1606) était un archevêque espagnol, missionnaire au Pérou et deuxième évêque de Lima – territoire qui à l’époque englobait le nord du Pérou dont Chiclayo. Un prédécesseur, en quelque sort, de Mgr Robert Prevost ! En fin d’après-midi, le 14 novembre, Léon XIV a retrouvé la communauté catholique de son ancien diocèse de Chiclayo, au sanctuaire de Santo Toribio de Mogrovejo, à Zaña. En ce lieu où mourut saint Toribio, le Pape s’est recueilli devant son ancienne tombe – désormais vide puisque sa dépouille repose dans la cathédrale de Lima. Léon XIV a ensuite participé à la clôture de l’année jubilaire marquant le troisième centenaire de la canonisation du missionnaire espagnol. Né à Mayorga, en Espagne, saint Toribio étudie le droit et devient un juriste réputé, professeur à l’université de Salamanque. Alors qu’il est encore laïc, le roi Philippe II le désigne pour devenir archevêque de Lima. summary_zh: 我叫 Martin Kilonzo 神父，ALCP/OSS。我是一名罗马天主教神父，也是圣神工团体（Opus Spiritus Sancti，简称ALCP/OSS）的司铎宗徒生活团体成员。我来自东非的肯尼亚，
title_zh: 隆重介绍圣若瑟天主教堂助理神父马丁·基隆佐（Martin Kilonzo）
content: My name is Fr. Martin Kilonzo, ALCP/OSS. I am a Roman Catholic priest and a member of the Apostolic Life Community of Priests in Opus Spiritus Sancti (ALCP/OSS). Originally from Kenya, East Africa, I currently serve as parochial vicar at St. Joseph’s Church in Devils Lake, N.D. My journey has been a remarkable experience of faith, formation, missionary service, and trust in God’s providence. I was born in 1978 in Kilenge, a small village in Makueni County, southeastern Kenya, where I attended elementary school. I later joined Pope Paul VI Minor Seminary in the Diocese of Machakos, my home diocese, where I received a high school education and spiritual formation that helped prepare me for the priesthood. After four years at the minor seminary, I pursued three years of philosophical studies at the Spiritan Missionary Seminary in Arusha, Tanzania, followed by four years of theological studies at Jordan University College in Morogoro, Tanzania. I was ordained a priest in July 2012 in the Diocese of Moshi, in Tanzania’s Kilimanjaro Region. Since my ordination, I have served in various pastoral assignments in Tanzania and Italy, enriching my missionary experience and understanding of different cultures. In 2026, following consultations between my religious superiors and the Bishop of Fargo, I was assigned to the Diocese of Fargo, N.D., beginning a new chapter in my priestly ministry. October 15 holds special significance for me as the anniversary of the day I first set foot on American soil. I arrived in Chicago before taking a connecting flight to Minot, N.D. After spending approximately one week serving at St. Mary’s Cathedral in Fargo, I was assigned to St. Joseph’s Church in Devils Lake, where I officially began my ministry as parochial vicar in February 2026. I consider my assignment in North Dakota a privilege and a renewed call to missionary service. Through God’s grace, I am grateful for the opportunity to celebrate the sacraments, provide spiritual guidance, and serve the parishioners of St. Joseph’s Church and the wider Devils Lake community, regardless of religious affiliation or background. For me, the journey from Kilenge, Kenya, to Devils Lake, N.D., is more than a change of place; it is a continuing response to God’s call to faith, service, and missionary discipleship with humility.

我叫马丁・基隆佐,ALCP/OSS。 我是一名罗马天主教神父,也是奥普斯·斯皮里图斯·桑茨蒂(ALCP/OSS)牧师的使徒生活社区的成员。 我最初来自肯尼亚、东非, 我的旅程在信仰、组织、传教仪式和对上帝之赐的信任方面,是非凡的经历。

1978年出生于肯尼亚东南部马库埃尼县的一个小村庄Kilenge,在那里就读小学. 我后来加入教宗保罗六世小神学院(Pope Paul VI Minor Seminary),参加我的家乡教区马查科斯教区,在那里我接受了高中教育和精神培养,帮助我为神职做好准备.

在小神学院学习了四年之后,我在坦桑尼亚阿鲁沙的Spiritan传教士神学院学习了三年哲学,之后在坦桑尼亚莫罗戈罗的约旦大学学院学习了四年神学。 我于2012年7月在坦桑尼亚乞力马扎罗大区莫希教区被任命为牧师。

自从我担任教职以来,我在坦桑尼亚和意大利从事各种牧业任务,丰富了我的传教经验和对不同文化的理解。 2026年,经我的宗教上司与法尔戈主教磋商,我被分配到北大法尔戈主教座堂,开始了我牧师部的新篇章.

10月15日是我第一次踏上美国土地的纪念日,对我来说具有特殊的意义. 我在搭乘连接航班去纽约州米诺特之前到达芝加哥 在法戈的圣玛丽大教堂服役约一周后,我被分配到魔鬼湖的圣约瑟教堂,2026年2月正式开始我的牧师部。

我将我在北达科他州的任务视为一种特权,也是对传教士服务的再次呼吁。 通过上帝的恩典,我感谢有机会庆祝圣训,提供精神指导,并为圣约瑟教堂的教友和更广泛的恶魔湖社区服务,而不论其宗教信仰或背景如何.

对我而言,从肯尼亚基伦格到N.D.D.的恶魔湖的旅程不仅仅是改变地方;它是对上帝发出的信仰、服务和谦逊的传教士的不断响应。

summary_zh: 面向传教教会的青年项目：Wecare。离开自己的家和“舒适区”几周，前往另一个国家，与他人共度时光、共同工作。
title_zh: 一个面向传教教会的青年项目：Wecare。
content: Un progetto giovane per la Chiesa missionaria: Wecare. Lasciare per alcune settimane la propria casa e le proprie “zone di conforto”, avventurarsi in un altro Paese e condividere tempo e lavoro con persone la cui vita è molto diversa. Per alcuni giovani, le vacanze possono trasformarsi in un’esperienza di incontri e di prossimità con realtà lontane. Dove, riferisce l’agenzia missionaria vaticana Fides, tutto può diventare occasione per interrogarsi su se stessi, sugli altri e sui desideri del proprio cuore. È quanto accade spesso nelle esperienze missionarie promosse da “Wecare”, una realtà italiana le cui radici risalgono a vent’anni fa e che ogni anno coinvolge numerosi giovani in progetti in Italia e in altri Paesi. La storia è iniziata nel 2005, quando Fernando Lozada Baldoceda, iniziatore delle esperienze di volontariato all’estero e oggi direttore di Wecare, organizzò un primo viaggio in Perù con tre universitari. “È stato il primo tentativo di un viaggio di volontariato”, ricorda. Nel 2006 l’esperienza ha iniziato a strutturarsi come gruppo e, negli anni successivi, è cresciuta fino a coinvolgere decine di giovani. Nel 2011 è stata creata una struttura giuridica per sostenere il progetto e, dopo diverse tappe e l’ampliamento delle attività anche in Italia, nel 2023 è nata Wecare nella forma che ha oggi. Per Fernando, più che l’evoluzione di un’organizzazione, questi vent’anni raccontano la storia di giovani che hanno scoperto di avere un tesoro da condividere, e hanno scelto di mettersi in gioco. Chiesa giovane “C’è molta più gioia nel dare che nel ricevere”, racconta Camilla di Roma a Fides. Dopo aver partecipato a un’esperienza in Argentina nel 2025 ha deciso di partire nuovamente quest’anno, questa volta per il Brasile. “Ho scelto di partecipare una seconda volta perché questa esperienza non aiuta soltanto gli altri, aiuta anche me- spiega-. Il contatto con gli altri permette di toccare corde di te che nella vita quotidiana non tocchi e di conoscersi in modo diverso”. In Brasile, uno degli incontri che più l’ha segnata è stato quello con la comunità di Milan dos Coelhos. “Ciò che mi ha colpito di più è stato l’amore che circondava la comunità”, ricorda. In particolare, l’ha colpita il modo in cui le persone si prendevano cura di Evinho, un anziano della comunità. Questo le ha fatto scoprire che, pur avendo molto poco, non mancava loro quello che per lei è il valore più importante: “L’amore per il prossimo, la prossimità e l’aiuto gratuito”. Al ritorno, quell’esperienza aveva cambiato anche il suo modo di guardare alla propria vita. “Sono tornata con una maggiore consapevolezza e con più voglia di aiutare gli altri- evidenzia-. L’esperienza ha ridimensionato le mie priorità e mi ha fatto comprendere meglio ciò per cui vale la pena lottare. Mi sento anche più grata per quello che ho e per ciò che mi circonda”. Anche Benedetta ha scelto di ripartire. Dopo il Perù nel 2022 e il Camerun nel 2025, quest’anno è tornata in Brasile. La frase “C’è più gioia nel dare che nel ricevere” ha accompagnato le sue esperienze. “Mi sento fortunata, ricevo molto ogni giorno e volevo capire che cosa significa davvero dare”, osserva.

title_zh: Lustre新闻
content: Dense fog blanketed our landscape on Nov. 1. The old timers say to expect some kind of precipitation 90 days from fog. That will be Feb. 1, 2027. Former pastor of the Lustre EMB Church, John Skillman, called to let our community know of the passing of Melody Nickel – Sharon's sister and wife of Missionary Dan Nickel – this morning in Ireland. Our deepest sympathies are extended to their families. Dan and Melody had been here in August as speakers of the recent Harvest Festival. They were long term missionaries in Ireland. Former LCHS teacher, Sarel Matthyser, passed away peacefully on Oct. 30, having lost his battle with cancer. He and his son, Josua had returned to South Africa to be with family. LCHS Foundation President Keith Unger emceed the Annual Foundation dinner. The LCHS Choir members served the meal of baked potatoes, brisket or barbecued pulled pork. Prizes were drawn and reports given. Keith introduced the speaker, Andy Shewey. He said the MB Foundation philosophy "is based on two principles: 1) God owns it all. (Ps 24:1) and 2) Therefore we are His stewards, seeking be rich in good works. (II Cor. 9:6-7, I Tim 6:17-19, Matthew 25)." He defined "heritage" as "something passed down from previous generations including cultural traditions, historical values, physical property and spiritual faith." Quoting David Green, CEO of Hobby Lobby, Mr. Shewey said "Legacy is what we set in motion." "Legacy is a last act of stewardship, reflecting your values, makes a statement and is a way to give past your own lifetime." He gave several family stories as examples of how generations were affected by how these people (in Kansas and Oklahoma) were "giving meaning to money." The evening was an encouragement to all who attended. The jamboree and junior high games of late have been exciting. The girls played Nashua at home Saturday evening, Frazer on Tuesday with Lustre Junior High girls winning in overtime by four, and on Friday travelled to Dodson to play the coyotes. The jamboree girls won 19-12, the jamboree boys lost 27-29 in a good game, the junior high girls won 31-18, and the junior high boys also won. The Frontier school comes Saturday to play at Lustre. Then it's Frazer and North Country next weekend, both at Lustre before the tournaments on Nov 20-21.

title: La Nación / La diócesis de San Lorenzo cuenta con nuevo obispo
summary: El papa León XIV nombró a monseñor Pierre Jubinville como nuevo obispo de la diócesis de San Lorenzo en reemplazo de monseñor Joaquín Robledo, quien presentó renuncia al cargo. La Nunciatura Apostólic

title_zh: 《国家报》/圣洛伦索教区迎来新主教
content: El papa León XIV nombró a monseñor Pierre Jubinville como nuevo obispo de la diócesis de San Lorenzo en reemplazo de monseñor Joaquín Robledo, quien presentó renuncia al cargo. La Nunciatura Apostólica en Paraguay comunicó el sábado 7 de noviembre que el santo padre aceptó la renuncia de Robledo y designó en su reemplazo a monseñor Pierre Laurent Jubinville, quien se desempeñaba como obispo de San Pedro y es el actual presidente de la Conferencia Episcopal Paraguaya (CEP). La decisión fue anunciada por la CEP, conforme a lo establecido en el Código de Derecho Canónico, que contempla la renuncia de los obispos al alcanzar los 75 años de edad. No obstante, monseñor Robledo continuará al frente de la diócesis como administrador apostólico hasta la toma de posesión canónica de su sucesor. La Conferencia Episcopal Paraguaya agradeció a monseñor Robledo por su servicio pastoral y dedicación a la Iglesia, al tiempo que encomendó en oración al nuevo obispo, deseándole un fecundo ministerio episcopal en su nueva misión. El nuevo obispo Monseñor Pierre Laurent Jubinville nació el 5 de agosto de 1960 en Ottawa, Canadá. Tras algunas experiencias laborales, ingresó en la Congregación del Espíritu Santo y estudió Teología en la Universidad de Montreal. Emitió los votos solemnes en 1988 y fue ordenado presbítero el 17 de setiembre de 1988. Tras algunas experiencias misioneras en África, realizó estudios académicos en Montreal y París. Llegó a Paraguay en 1991, desarrolló diversas tareas pastorales y formativas; entre ellas, se desempeñó en la pastoral indígena de la parroquia San José Obrero, en la Diócesis de San Pedro; fue párroco de San Francisco de Asís y formador de la Congregación del Espíritu Santo en Asunción. En 2013 fue nombrado obispo de San Pedro y recibió la ordenación episcopal el 21 de diciembre de ese mismo año. Además, ejerció la vicepresidencia de la Conferencia Episcopal Paraguaya entre 2018 y 2024 y, desde noviembre de 2024, ocupa la presidencia de dicha institución. La Diócesis de San Lorenzo comprende varias localidades del departamento Central, entre ellas Capiatá, San Lorenzo, Ñemby, Itá, Ypané, Guarambaré, Villeta, Nueva Italia, San Antonio, J. Augusto Saldívar, Ypacaraí y Thompson.

title: Pope warns of dehumanization caused by AI
summary: Pope Leo XIV waves to faithful from the popemobile upon his arrival for a prayer vigil at the Centenario Stadium in Montevideo on November 7, 2026. (AFP Photo) Pope Leo XIV warned students on Nov. 7 o
summary_zh: 2026年11月7日，教宗利奥十四世抵达蒙得维的亚百年体育场参加祈祷守夜活动，他在教宗座驾上向信众挥手致意。（法新社照片）教宗利奥十四世于11月7日告诫学生们
title_zh: 教皇警告人工智能会导致非人性化
content: Pope Leo XIV waves to faithful from the popemobile upon his arrival for a prayer vigil at the Centenario Stadium in Montevideo on November 7, 2026. (AFP Photo) Pope Leo XIV warned students on Nov. 7 of “dehumanization” through the use of AI in education, and urged schools and university to place the “person before the algorithm.” “The process of dehumanization we are experiencing poses a challenge,” the pope, who has warned repeatedly about the need to ensure AI is used ethically, said in a speech at the Catholic University of Uruguay. Just three weeks after undergoing surgery for lung cancer, the 71-year-old pontiff is on a 12-day tour of South Africa where he served nearly two decades as a missionary. On Nov. 7, he visited the crime-blighted Montevideo neighborhood of Casavalle. The murder rate in the impoverished district is four times the national average and residents spoke movingly of the dangers they faced, like commonplace gun violence. Katherine Silva’s voice cracked with emotion as she told the pope about the violence and abuse she had suffered as a child. After ending up homeless at 15, the young mother said she “went through very dark times” and “nearly died.” “There are children in Uruguay who do not go to school for fear of never returning home,” Leo said. “In a country as rich in resources as this, children should never have to go to bed hungry... Much less should they have to suffer violence to the point of losing their lives,” he added. As police helicopters flew overhead, locals waved and cheered to welcome the head of the world’s 1.4 billion Catholics, who blessed 12 new low-income houses financed by the Church.
content_zh:
教皇利奥十四世于2026年11月7日抵达蒙得维的亚百人马体育场举行祈祷仪式时,从教皇座堂向忠实者挥手. (AFP Photo)教宗利奥十四在11月警告学生.

在教育中运用AI, 教皇在乌拉圭天主教大学的演讲中反复警告,需要确保AI在道德上得到使用。

在接受肺癌手术三周后,71岁的庞蒂夫正在南非进行为期12天的考察,他作为传教士服务了近20年。 11月7日,他访问了Casavalle的蒙得维的亚犯罪街区。

贫困地区的谋杀率是全国平均水平的四倍,居民们感动地谈到他们所面临的危险,如普通的枪支暴力。 Katherine Silva告诉教皇她小时候遭受的暴力和虐待,

年轻母亲15岁就无家可归, Leo说:“乌拉圭有些儿童因为害怕永远不回家而不去上学。” “在一个资源如此丰富的国家里,儿童永远不应挨饿。 他补充说,他们更不应该遭受暴力,以至于失去生命。”

summary_zh: 文：查尔斯·加德纳（Charles Gardner）——一位勇敢的也门记者讲述了他在访问以色列后，对以色列的看法发生了翻天覆地的变化，这一说法令联合国感到震惊。他得出的结论是，他被教导要相信的关于犹太人的所有事情都是谎言。鲁艾·艾哈迈德应邀 […]  这篇文章《也门记者访问以色列，观点发生巨大转变》最初发表在《上帝报道》上。
title_zh: 也门记者访问以色列，观点发生戏剧性变化
content: By Charles Gardner — Luai Ahmed speaking at UN (screenshot YouTube) A brave Yemeni journalist has stunned the United Nations with an account of how his view of Israel has dramatically changed following a visit there. And he was led to the conclusion that everything he has been taught to believe about the Jews is a lie. Luai Ahmed was invited to address the assembly by UN Watch, a non-governmental organisation monitoring the international body’s performance, as the UN Human Rights Council gathered to debate racism. He said: “I grew up in Yemen, where the word that we used for black people is ‘abeed’, which quite literally means ‘slaves’. Racism towards black people in my country is horrifying, but it’s not even the most toxic hatred that I was taught. “The first time I ever heard the word ‘Jew’ was in my local mosque when I was nine years old. At the end of Friday prayers, the Imam said: ‘May Allah kill the Jews and the Zionists’. And I responded alongside thousands of Muslims praying beside me: ‘Ameen’.” Luai then continued: “I was taught that Zionism meant killing Arabs, stealing our land, and destroying Islam. Then October 7th came. Hamas terrorists ‘freed Palestine’ by slaughtering 1,200 Israelis and kidnapping more than 200 people, including a one-year-old child. “Almost everyone in my Arab-Muslim circle celebrated. I didn’t. Instead, as a journalist, I decided to visit the so-called Zionist entity, and I was completely shocked to the core by the lack of apartheid and racism that I experienced. “One day, I got an eye infection. At the hospital, the nurses in reception were Jewish. The doctor treating me was Arab. Is there racism in Israel? Of course. There’s racism everywhere. “But Arabs in Israel aren’t called ‘slaves’. They are doctors, engineers, and party leaders. My experience helped me realise that Zionism really just means the Jewish people’s right to a tiny country. Everything I was taught was a lie.” Quite apart from tipping over the tables of woke left-wing ideology spreading its poisonous antisemitic tentacles across the globe, Luai’s testimony also knocks holes into the escalating pressure on the UK to make reparations for the slave trade, which saw plenty of collaborators in the host countries of those who suffered. And of course, the truth that dare not speak its name – that it was Christians like William Wilberforce who put an end to it! Luai is a great inspiration to fellow journalists like me who long for more of our colleagues to stand up and be counted. Thanks also to David Soakell of Christian Friends of Israel’s Watching Over Zion newsletter, November 5, 2026. The post Yemeni journalist visits Israel, dramatically changes views first appeared on God Reports .
content_zh:
一位勇敢的也门记者在联合国(YouTube)讲话时, 而他由此得出了这样的结论:他所学的关于犹太人的一切信仰都是谎言.

Luai Ahmed被联合国观察组织邀请在大会上讲话,该组织是监测国际机构业绩的非政府组织,在联合国人权理事会聚集一堂讨论种族主义问题。 他说:“我成长于也门, 我们用来形容黑人的字眼是“有病”的,

对我国黑人的种族主义令人恐惧, “当我九岁时,我第一次听到`犹太人'这个词是在我的地方清真寺。 星期五祷告结束时,教母说:愿真主杀害犹太教徒和犹太复国主义者。

我与数千名穆斯林一同祈祷: 卢艾接着说:“我被告知犹太复国主义意味着杀害阿拉伯人、偷窃我们的土地并摧毁伊斯兰教。 后于十月七日来. 哈马斯恐怖分子屠杀了1 200名以色列人并绑架了200多人,包括一名一岁儿童,从而“解放了巴勒斯坦”。 “我的阿拉伯-穆斯林圈子里几乎每个人都庆祝。

我没有。 相反,作为一名记者,我决定访问所谓的犹太复国主义实体,我对缺乏种族隔离和种族主义感到完全震惊。 “有一天,我眼睛受到感染。 在医院接待的护士是犹太人. 治疗我的医生是阿拉伯人。 以色列是否存在种族主义? 当然 到处都有种族主义。

“但以色列的阿拉伯人并不被称为奴隶。 他们是医生、工程师和党领袖。 我的经验帮助我意识到犹太复国主义只是意味着犹太人民对一个小国的权利。

我所学的一切都是谎言。” 卢艾的证言不仅在醒目的左翼意识形态席上倾出,在全球散布出有毒的反酋长触角,还打入了英国为奴隶贸易提供赔偿的不断升级的压力的洞口,在那些受苦受难者所在的东道国中,有许多合作者。

当然,那个不敢说出自己名字的真理——是威廉·威尔伯福斯这样的基督徒终结了它! 吕艾对像我这样的记者同事来说是一个巨大的灵感,他们渴望有更多的同事站起起来被统计. 也感谢以色列基督教之友的David Soakell,

title_zh: 蝠鲼带领海洋科学家找到失去的鳍
content: By Mark Ellis — Amber Sparks (Blue Latitudes Foundation Facebook page) Growing up in Laguna Beach, California, Amber Sparks developed a deep love for the ocean, which led her to study marine science at UC Berkeley and earn a master’s degree at Scripps Institute in San Diego. As co-founder of Blue Latitudes Foundation, she works with industry to find opportunities for conservation, especially with the Rigs-to-Reefs program, when oil drilling platforms are decommissioned. “We work with the oil companies to repurpose certain parts of the platform, retrofit it so that it can remain in place and continue to function as an artificial reef,” she told God Reports. Amber’s work has taken her around the world, with many dive experiences and encounters in the ocean with marine life. But there is one story she will never forget. It happened in the Gulf of Mexico shortly after Amber graduated from Scripps Institute and was invited on a research industry cruise with oil company representatives, scientists, and regulators on a liveaboard vessel. At the Flower Garden National Banks, a marine protected area 200 miles offshore, Amber was excited about her first dive, but slightly nervous. “You don’t know what you’re going to see or what this experience is going to be like,” she recalls. Dropping in (Blue Latitudes Foundation Facebook) Each diver had to jump off the vessel to get in the water. “We’re all geared up with our snorkel, our buoyancy control device, our wetsuit, and fins are the last thing you put on. So, I put on my fins and I jumped off the side of the boat.” “The second that I hit the water, one of my fins fell off, and I looked down and watched as it slowly descended to the bottom.” Amber glanced over at her dive buddy, and said, “I’m gonna go down. I’m going down.” Normally she would wait for her dive partner and they would go down together, but in this case, she thought, “I can’t (wait). I gotta go get my fin.” So Amber slowly began to descend to the bottom, about 60 feet below the ocean surface. “I felt completely lost. I was in a completely new area. I never dove before, and now I only had one fin.” She realized there were major currents that could have moved her fin in any direction. “I realized I can’t really swim with just one fin. So now not only am I at depth, but I’m handicapped with just one fin, and I started to feel pretty nervous.” It would probably take her 10 minutes to get back the surface, with safety stops. At the moment before panic set in, she looked upward and saw an amazing sight. It was a giant manta ray, with wings extending at least 10 feet. “Its wingspan was double mine. Its arms were out, and it was coming up over the side of a reef. “I’ve never seen a manta ray like this before. It totally took my breath away, it was so magnificent.” Another manta ray (Blue Latitudes Foundation Facebook page) She noted that manta rays are known in the ocean community to be “majestic, God-connected creatures with an understanding maybe beyond what humans can fully comprehend. They see the world and feel it in another way,” she notes. Mantas have the largest known brain of any fish. Their brains are large in absolute terms and relative to body size, which is also true of elephants, dolphins, and people. Their brains have enlarged areas associated with intelligence, vision, and motor coordination, and some of their brain cells are more like those in birds and mammals than in other fish.(1) As the manta ray drew close to Amber, she had an unusual communication experience. “I felt this sense where it said, ‘I want you to follow me. I’m going to help you find your fin.’ Amber Sparks Amber’s diving partner had just descended next to her, and they both began to swim after the manta. “I was barely making it, following this manta ray across the reef. title_zh: 拉尼尔第六届年度约翰·沃里克·蒙哥马利系列讲座：圆满成功
content: John Warwick Montgomery While sitting in the John Warwick Montgomery Study Center at the Lanier Library and Study Center in Houston, Texas, awaiting a meeting, I turned to librarian Sharon Cofran and Executive Director Dr. David Fleming and remarked, “John Warwick Montgomery would be very pleased with what Lanier has accomplished on his behalf.” From Montgomery’s framed correspondence with C. S. Lewis and his barrister gowns to the thousands of books that comprise his remarkable personal collection, Lanier has provided the Christian world with a marvelous tribute to one of the great Christian intellectuals of the twentieth and twenty-first centuries. Born in 1931, John Warwick Montgomery (d. 2024) was a distinguished Christian apologist, theologian, attorney, and scholar whose extraordinary career spanned several disciplines. Holding numerous academic degrees, including doctorates in theology, philosophy, and law, Montgomery became internationally recognized for his defense of Christianity through historical evidence, legal reasoning, and philosophical argumentation. His influential books, including History and Christianity , Faith Founded on Fact , and The Shape of the Past , helped establish a rigorous approach to Christian apologetics. Whether lecturing in universities, debating skeptics, or practicing law, Montgomery maintained that Christianity was not merely a matter of subjective belief but a faith grounded in historical reality and rational inquiry. Yet to stop at the library would be to understate Lanier’s remarkable work. The sixth annual John Warwick Montgomery Lecture Series was a tour de force of distinguished thinkers, passionate Christians, and intellectually engaging presentations. More than a commemoration of Montgomery’s life, the gathering represented a continuation of his intellectual legacy: the conviction that Christianity can withstand serious scrutiny and offer compelling answers to life’s most profound questions. Mark Lanier, Nancy Pearcey, Paul Gould, Adam Francisco, and Michael Horton From the opening panel discussion hosted by attorney and philanthropist Mark Lanier to Dr. Paul Gould’s thoughtful presentation on worldviews, followed by attorney Craig Parton’s lecture on jurisprudential apologetics, one theme emerged with unmistakable clarity: Christianity is a reasonable faith. The presentations reflected Montgomery’s own interdisciplinary approach to apologetics: the Christian faith and intellectual inquiry need not be adversaries. Indeed, the Christian tradition has long insisted that faith and reason are complementary avenues in the pursuit of truth. The following day continued this rich intellectual exploration. Professor Nancy Pearcey addressed questions surrounding truth, dismantling various modern ideologies, while Dr. Adam Francisco offered an informative overview of Islamic history and belief, helping participants better understand one of world’s biggest religions. The keynote address by Dr. Michael Horton examined the challenge of reaching those who identify as “spiritual but not religious,” a growing segment of contemporary society. Horton’s presentation underscored the importance of communicating historic Christian truth in a culture increasingly suspicious of religious institutions yet often deeply interested in spiritual meaning. Dr. Michael Horton On Sunday morning, Lanier founder, Mark Lanier, hosted many participants during his Biblical literacy class, where he continued the dialogue with Michael Horton. Taken together, the lectures, discussions, and interviews demonstrated the breadth of Christian scholarship and the continuing relevance of thoughtful apologetics in an age of skepticism, religious pluralism, and cultural uncertainty. As I reflected on the weekend, I was reminded of the Festschrift Christianity for the Tough-Minded , a collection of scholarly essays honoring Montgomery’s life and ministry. Like that volume, the Lanier lecture series brought together diverse intellec

约翰·沃里克·蒙哥马利 在德克萨斯州休斯敦拉尼尔图书馆和研究中心的约翰·沃里克·蒙哥马利研究中心等待开会时,我找图书管理员沙龙·科夫兰和执行主任戴维·弗莱明博士说:“约翰·沃里克·蒙哥马利将非常高兴拉尼尔代表他取得的成就。” 蒙哥马利与C.S.的书信

刘易斯和他的大律师礼服为他杰出的个人收藏的数千本书,为基督教世界向20世纪和21世纪伟大的基督教知识分子之一致敬。 1931年出生于约翰·沃里克·蒙哥马利(d.

2024年)是一位杰出的基督教道歉学家,神学家,律师和学者,其非凡的事业跨越多个学科. 蒙哥马利拥有众多学术学位,包括神学,哲学和法学的博士学位,他通过历史证据,法律推理,哲学论证,为基督教辩护而获得国际承认.

他的有影响力的著作,包括历史和基督教、基于事实的信仰、以及过去的造型,帮助确立了对基督教学的严格态度。 无论是在大学里讲课,辩论怀疑论,还是执业法律,蒙哥马利都坚持认为基督教不仅仅是主观信仰的问题,而是建立在历史现实和理性调查基础上的信仰.

然而, 停留在图书馆将会低估拉尼尔的出色工作。 第六届年度约翰·沃里克·蒙哥马利讲座系列是由杰出的思想家,充满热情的基督徒,以及智力参与的演讲组成的巡回演出.

这场集会不仅仅是纪念蒙哥马利的一生,它代表着他思想遗产的延续:相信基督教能够经受住严肃的审视,为人生最深刻的问题提供令人信服的答案.

马克·拉尼尔 南希·皮尔西 保罗·古尔德 亚当·弗朗西斯科 迈克尔·霍顿 从律师和慈善家马克·拉尼尔主持的开场小组讨论到保罗·古尔德博士关于世界观的深思熟虑的演讲,然后是克雷格·帕顿律师关于法学理论的演讲,一个主题以明确无误的方式出现: 基督教是一种合理的信仰.

这些介绍反映了蒙哥马利自己对学说采取的跨学科方法:基督教信仰和知识调查不必是对手。 事实上,基督教传统长期以来一直坚持信仰和理性是追求真理的补充途径。 次日继续进行这种丰富的知识探索.

Nancy Pearcey教授谈到了围绕真理的问题,摧毁了各种现代意识形态,而Adam Francisco博士则提供了伊斯兰历史和信仰的翔实概览,帮助与会者更好地理解世界上最大的宗教之一。 由Dr.A.先生作主旨发言。

迈克尔·霍顿研究了帮助那些认为是“精神上但并非宗教上”的当代社会日益扩大的阶层的挑战。 霍顿的演讲强调了在一种对宗教机构越来越怀疑、但往往对精神意义很感兴趣的文化中传播基督教历史真理的重要性。 医生

讲座、讨论和访谈共同显示了基督教奖学金的广度,以及深思熟虑的学说在怀疑主义、宗教多元化和文化不确定性的时代的持续相关性。

summary_zh: 文：查尔斯·加德纳（Charles Gardner）——在第二次世界大战南太平洋的一场海战中，一名日本水兵所在的驱逐舰被美国人击沉，他的大多数战友都淹死了。令人惊奇的是，尽管鱼雷官新谷通晴与其他人一起被卷入波涛之下，随着战舰的沉没，但他却奇迹般地在这场1942年的灾难中幸存下来。（只有18名……）  这篇文章《二战日本战俘在战俘营中找到“自由”》最初发表在《上帝报道》上。
title_zh: 二战日本战俘在战俘营中找到“自由”
content: By Charles Gardner — When a Japanese sailor’s destroyer was sunk by the Americans in a World War II South Pacific battle, most of his companions drowned. Amazingly, even though he was sucked underneath the waves with others as the ship went down, torpedo officer Michiharu Shinya somehow survived this 1942 disaster. (Only 18 of the 200-strong crew did). But he would rather have died at that point as his people had been indoctrinated to believe that it was shameful to be captured. Nevertheless, he was badly wounded but nursed back to health by medics. In time, he was picked up and eventually taken to a Prisoner-of-War camp at Featherston, near Wellington, in New Zealand, where he was to spend the next three years, as Don Stephens records in his inspirational book War and Grace (Evangelical Press, an imprint of 10Publishing). Shinya and his fellow inmates were treated with much kindness (in sharp contrast to the torture often experienced by Allied prisoners at the hands of the Japanese). Being showered with gifts at Christmas, a feast he knew nothing about, seemed especially strange. However, he was determined not to be ‘taken in’ by the Christian teaching offered after some of the prisoners requested spiritual help and a Japanese Bible was made available. That is until he chanced upon an article entitled ‘Sorrow in Victory’ in which the author quoted a ‘Hebrew prophet’ as saying: “Those who hope in the Lord will renew their strength. They shall soar on wings like eagles; they will run and not grow weary; they will walk and not be faint.” It made a deep impression on him, and he was determined to find out where it came from. Assuming it was from the Old Testament, he began reading the Bible, starting at Genesis chapter 1. Eventually, to his joy, he discovered that the profound words were from the Book of the prophet Isaiah (chapter 40, verse 31). After flagging somewhat in his search, he found himself hospitalised with malaria when a friend brought him a booklet called The Reason Why explaining the way to salvation. It so happened that the camp’s chaplain, Pastor Hessell Troughton, had been a missionary to Japan and spoke the language. Shinya joined others in his Bible studies and came to know and love Jesus as his Saviour. So much did this “complete freedom” now rule his life that prison had morphed into what he described as “a unique paradise on earth”. He never looked back after that and became convinced that his post-war calling would be in service of his Lord. When he finally returned home, his family were shocked to see him alive for he had been reported as killed in action. He had also given a false name to his captors because of the supposed shame of falling into enemy hands. Shinya subsequently became a pastor and prolific writer and translator following years of theological study both in Tokyo and the US. The Old Testament, he came to believe, demonstrated that sin is “the ultimate problem of mankind” and clearly pointed to Christ as the answer. On seeking to understand why so few Japanese became Christians, he felt it was partly due to their pride borne of believing they were a superior race. As for those three Christmases he spent in New Zealand, author Don Stephens writes: “Of all the gifts he received, the one he valued most was ‘the boundless and deep grace and peace of God in the Lord Jesus Christ’.” The post WWII Japanese POW found ‘freedom’ in camp first appeared on God Reports .
content_zh:
查尔斯·加德纳编著: 当一艘日本水手的驱逐舰在二战南太平洋战役中被美国人击沉时,大部分同伴溺毙. 令人惊奇的是,尽管随着船只的下沉,他与其他人一起被吸在海浪下,但鱼雷军官Michiharu Shinya却不知何故幸免于1942年的灾难。 (200人的船员中只有18人这样做).

但他宁愿死在那个时候,因为他的族人被灌输相信被俘虏是可耻的. 然而,他受了重伤,但被医护人员喂养。

在时间上,他被接了起来,最终被带到新西兰惠灵顿附近的费瑟斯顿(Featherston)的战俘营,在那里他将度过接下来的三年,正如唐·斯蒂芬斯在他的励志书"战争与格蕾丝"(福音出版社,10Publishing的印记)中记载的那样.

信也和同狱囚犯受到很大程度的善待(与盟军囚犯经常在日本人手中遭受的酷刑形成鲜明对比). 在圣诞节用礼物淋浴 一个他一无所知的宴会 看起来特别奇怪

然而,在一些囚犯要求精神帮助和提供日本圣经后,他决心不再接受基督教教义的 " 接纳 " 。 直到他看到一篇题为“为胜利而悲伤”的文章,作者在文章中引用了一位“赫布鲁先知”的话:“那些希望主复活的人。 他们将像鹰一样飞翔,

他们将奔驰,而不会疲倦,他们将走路,而不会晕倒。 这给他留下了深刻的印象,他下定决心要找出它来自何处. 假设它来自旧约,他开始阅读圣经,从创世纪第一章开始. 最终,在他的喜悦中,他发现深刻的文字来自先知以赛亚的经典(第40章第31节).

在搜索中略微浮出水面后,他发现自己患上了疟疾,一位朋友给他带了一本小册子,名为《原因》,解释救世之路。 难民营的牧师Hessell Troughton牧师曾是日本的传教士, 信也加入了其他人的圣经研究,来到了了解和热爱耶稣作为他的救世主.

这种“完全自由”现在统治了他的生活,监狱变成了他所称的“地球上独一无二的天堂”。 他从此之后再也没有回头看,并且确信他的战后召唤将会为他的主服务. 当他最终回家时,家人震惊地看到他活着,因为他被报道为阵亡.

他还给抓捕者取了一个假名,因为被假定是落入敌人手中的耻辱。 在东京和美国多年的神学研究之后,信也后来成为一名牧师和多产作家和翻译。 他逐渐相信,《旧约》表明了罪恶是“人类的最终问题”,并明确指出基督是答案。

在试图理解为什么如此少的日本人成为基督徒时,他感到部分是由于他们的自豪感,因为他们相信他们是优越的种族。

至于他在新西兰度过的三个圣诞节,作者Don Stephens写道:"在他收到的所有礼物中,他最珍视的一件是`上帝在耶稣基督中无限和深厚的恩惠与和平 ' 。 日本战俘在营地发现「自由」,

title_zh: 在西部明星的阴影下：格罗弗·刘易斯、拉里·麦克默特里和文字的胜利
content: With The Grover Lewis Reader: Splendor in the Short Grass and Western Star , the newest biography of Larry McMurtry, in hand, I load my truck and head toward Archer City, Texas, accompanied by my wife, Melanie, and our friend Eliott. Archer City is, of course, McMurtry country, a small Texas town made famous through the literary imagination of one of America’s most celebrated novelists. Having written about McMurtry’s faith—or lack thereof—in a previous article , following an earlier visit to Archer City, I’m returning with a somewhat different interest. This time, my attention turns to Grover Lewis, the gifted journalist, critic, and poet whose life intersected with McMurtry’s during their college years. Lewis’ story, however, begins not with literary achievement but with almost unimaginable tragedy. As a child, he experienced the devastating loss of both parents when his father murdered his mother and was subsequently shot with the same gun, either by his dying wife or another person present. Lewis was only eight years old. It is difficult to imagine a more horrific beginning. Yet rather than allowing that tragedy to become the entirety of his story, Lewis eventually found a voice through literature. Perhaps the cards life dealt him gave him plenty to write about. Or perhaps writing became his way of making sense of a world that had revealed its cruelty far too early. In his autobiographical poem “Hillbilly Song,” Lewis writes: “You asked me once, Ann/Over coffee gone cold with talk/In your mother’s rain-drowsy/House, who they were, how it/Was with them in their breathless/Time in the wilds of years.” For Lewis, those early years were indeed wild. But they were also the soil from which his literary imagination would eventually grow. A Life in Words Born in Texas in 1934, Grover Lewis emerged as a distinctive voice in American journalism, particularly through his cultural criticism and reporting on the rapidly changing landscape of the 1960s and 1970s. He became known for his sharp observations, literary flair, and ability to capture the personalities and contradictions of American culture, even if he occasionally stretched the truth in the telling. His work appeared in prominent publications, including Rolling Stone , where his reporting helped establish his reputation as an insightful, sometimes cutting observer of popular culture. Lewis was more than a journalist, however. He was a poet and literary craftsman, someone who understood that words could do more than convey information. They could illuminate the human condition, expose its contradictions, and perhaps even provide a measure of healing. Grover Lewis (ChatPGT) Continuing “Hillbilly Song,” Lewis ponders: “At last, breathless and dry-mouthed/With private desire in the blue,/Swollen dark, we all lie down together—/My mother, my father, their perishing/Dreams, and I this unborn prisoner son…” There is something haunting about these lines. The dead remain present. The past refuses to disappear. And the poet, even as an adult, seems to wrestle with the circumstances that shaped his entrance into the world. Yet the very act of writing suggests something else: a refusal to remain silent. Two Texans, Two Literary Paths Lewis and Larry McMurtry crossed paths as students at North Texas State College, now the University of North Texas, during the 1950s. Both were young Texans drawn to literature and the possibilities of the written word. Their friendship developed within a shared intellectual environment, one that encouraged reading, conversation, and the pursuit of literary ambitions. Although their careers eventually followed different paths—McMurtry toward novels, screenplays, and literary fame, Lewis toward journalism, poetry, and cultural criticism—they shared an interest in the complexities of American life. 与《格罗弗·刘易斯读者:短草中的辉煌与西部之星》,拉里·麦克默特里的最新传记, 手持,我装载我的卡车并前往德克萨斯州阿彻城, 由我的妻子梅兰妮和我们的朋友埃利奥特陪同。 阿彻城当然是麦克默特里国家,一个通过美国最著名的小说家之一的文学想象而成名的德克萨斯小镇.

在之前访问Archer城后, 我对McMurtry的信仰(或缺乏信仰)有一番兴趣, 这一次,我转而关注有天赋的记者、评论家和诗人格罗弗·刘易斯,他在大学时代的生活与麦克默特里的生活交织在一起。

然而,刘易斯的故事并非从文学成就开始,而是从几乎难以想象的悲剧开始. 他从小就经历了父母的惨痛损失,当时他的父亲谋杀了他的母亲,随后被他即将死亡的妻子或在场的其他人用同一把枪射杀。 刘易斯才八岁 很难想象一个更可怕的开端。

然而,刘易斯最终没有让这场悲剧成为他的全部故事,而是通过文学找到了声音. 也许他命中注定的卡片 给他写了很多东西 或写作成为他理解世界的方式, 这个世界已经揭示了它的残酷性,还为时过早。

刘易斯在自传诗“Hillbilly Song”中写道 : “ 你曾经问过我,Ann/Over咖啡随着谈话而变得冷淡,在你妈妈的雨滴/住所里,他们是谁,他们在无气息的年代/在野外时如何。 ” 对刘易斯来说,那些早年的确很狂野. 但它们也是他的文学想象最终会成长的土壤.

1934年出生于德克萨斯州的"言语生活"(A Life in Words Born in Texas),格罗弗·刘易斯(Grover Lewis)成为美国新闻业中一个有特色的代言人,特别是通过他对1960年代和1970年代迅速变化的地貌的文化批评和报道.

他以尖锐的观察,文学的才华,以及能够捕捉美国文化的个性和矛盾而闻名,即使他偶尔在讲述中伸张真理. 他的作品出现在包括滚石公司在内的著名出版物中,他的报道帮助他树立了自己作为有见地,有时剪切流行文化观察者的声誉.

然而,刘易斯不只是一名记者。 他是一位诗人和文学家,一个懂得文字可以比传递信息更有用的人. 它们可以揭示人类的状况,暴露其矛盾,甚至可能提供某种治疗方法。

Grover Lewis (ChatPGT) 继续“Hillbilly Song,” 刘易斯思考道:“最后,无气息和干燥的嘴唇/在蓝色的暗处私欲下,我们都躺在一起——/我的母亲、父亲、他们的死亡/梦想,我这个未出生的囚犯儿子......” 这些台词有些困扰。 死者仍然在场。 过去拒绝消失。

而诗人,即使作为一个成年人,似乎也与塑造他进入世界的环境相搏. 然而,写作本身就暗示了另一种情况:拒绝保持沉默。 两德克萨斯州立大学,两条文学道路刘易斯州立大学和拉里·麦克默特里(英语:Larry McMurtry)在1950年代作为北德克萨斯州立学院,即现在的北德克萨斯大学的学生跨过道路.

两人都是年轻的德克萨斯人,被吸引到文学和写字的可能性. 他们的友谊是在共同的知识环境中发展起来的,这种环境鼓励阅读,对话,追求文学野心.

summary: By Charles Gardner — A Jewish army surgeon was amazed by the courage of a young soldier badly wounded in the Battle of Gettysburg during the American Civil War (1861-65). Dr Max Rossvally was forced to amputate both a leg and arm in a bid to save the boy’s life. But it changed his own […]  The post  Jewish army doctor turned to Jesus after witnessing patient’s courage  first appeared on  God Reports .
summary_zh: 文：查尔斯·加德纳（Charles Gardner）——一位犹太籍陆军外科医生对一名年轻士兵的勇气感到惊叹，这名士兵在美国内战（1861-65）的葛底斯堡战役中身受重伤。为了挽救这个男孩的生命，马克斯·罗斯瓦利（Max Rossvally）博士不得不截肢，截掉了他的一条腿和一条胳膊。但这改变了他自己……  这篇题为《犹太军医在目睹病人的勇气后归向耶稣》的文章  最初发表在《上帝报道》上。
title_zh: 犹太军医在目睹病人的勇气后归信耶稣
content: Pastor Peter Colon portraying Major Rossvally in the movie of his story By Charles Gardner — A Jewish army surgeon was amazed by the courage of a young soldier badly wounded in the Battle of Gettysburg during the American Civil War (1861-65). Dr Max Rossvally was forced to amputate both a leg and arm in a bid to save the boy’s life. But it changed his own life. For the 17-year-old Drummer Boy – too young for frontline duty – refused chloroform or brandy to dull the pain. Charlie Coulson chose instead to trust in Jesus, his Lord and Saviour. The doctor – an army major and Orthodox Jew – was understandably stunned by the boy’s bravery, as well as his boldness in declaring his faith in Christ and imploring the officer (whom he knew to be Jewish) to put his own trust in Jesus, since he was also the Jewish Messiah. Max, however, was shaken rigid, and in a great dilemma, as he had always been taught to hate Jesus. For his people had largely rejected him as an ‘impostor’ and false Messiah. Charlie died just days later, apparently more concerned for the doctor’s eternal destiny than for his own painful exit from this life. Ten years later, Max found himself in a barber’s chair in New York once more being urged to trust in Jesus. Having explained the gospel, the barber promised to pray for him and said that, whenever he came in contact with a Jew, he felt it his duty to introduce him to the one who came for “the lost sheep of Israel” (Matthew 10:6). The surgeon subsequently boarded a train for a business meeting in Washington, where a newspaper advertisement drew him to a ‘revival’ service where the preacher echoed the messages he had heard from the barber and the boy soldier, leaving him in tears. He agonised at home in prayer for some time afterwards, struggling most of all with the thought that, if he accepted Christ, he would be going against all the advice and teaching he had known, not to mention the Jewish community as a whole. But he finally became convinced that Jesus was indeed the fulfilment of Old Testament prophecies (in particular, Genesis 49:10, Micah 5:2 and Isaiah 7:14). So he prayed: “O Lord God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. You know I am sincere in this thing. If Jesus Christ is the Son of God, reveal him to me this night, and I will accept him as my Messiah.” A long battle ensued, but his doubts were eventually replaced by joy and happiness as he praised God that he had found the true Shiloh, Ruler of Israel and Emmanuel. He was to pay a high price, however, as do all who follow Christ. His wife walked out on him; his parents disowned him. But he never gave up hope as he constantly prayed and reached out to his family. After 54 days, his wife joined him as a disciple of Jesus and, in time, his daughter also became a believer. But his son disowned him for many years until he was eventually reconciled both with his earthly and heavenly Father. In an extraordinary sequel some 18 months after he came to Christ, Max met up with Mrs Coulson, the mother of his dying young patient all those years earlier on the battlefield. With great joy, he was able to share how her son had set him on the path to a glorious future in Christ, which was to touch lives across the world, including my home county of Yorkshire in England. In fact, he came to live in Leeds to reach out to the Jewish community there and is buried at Lawnswood Cemetery in the city. An Irish friend of mine, Colin Nevin, has visited the grave, which includes an excerpt from one of the doctor’s hymns, I am Coming Soon, and was able to give a copy of Max’s story to a caretaker, so continuing the evangelist’s legacy more than a century after his death in 1892, aged 64. A 54-minute movie – Rossvally: From the Synagogue to the Saviour – has been produced on DVD and can apparently be ordered online. content_zh:
牧师彼得·科隆在他的故事电影"查尔斯·加德纳"(By Charles Gardner)中描绘了罗斯瓦利少校——一位犹太军队外科医生对美国内战期间格底斯堡战役(1861-65)中一名年轻士兵严重受伤的勇气感到惊讶. Max Rossvally医生被迫截肢, 但这改变了他自己的生活。

对于17岁的Drummer Boy — — 年龄太小,无法承担前线任务 — — 拒绝氯仿或白兰地来消磨疼痛。 查理·科尔森选择了信任耶稣,他的主和救世主.

这位医生是一名陆军少校和正统犹太人,对男孩的勇敢以及他大胆地宣布对基督的信仰,恳求军官(他知道是犹太人)相信耶稣是可以理解的,因为他也是犹太弥赛亚。 然而,马克思被动摇僵硬,陷入了巨大的困境,因为他一直被教导要憎恨耶稣.

他的宗族曾否认他是一个 " 骗子 " 和假的弥赛亚。 Charlie在几天后就去世了,显然更关心医生的永恒命运,而不是他自己痛苦地离开这一生。 10年后,马克思发现自己在纽约的理发师座椅上再次被敦促信任耶稣.

在解释了福音之后,理发师答应为他祈祷,并说每当他与一个犹太人接触时,他觉得有义务将他介绍给前来寻找“迷失的以色列羊”的人(Matthew 10:6)。

外科医生随后登上火车在华盛顿举行商务会议,报纸的广告将他引向 " 复活 " 服务,传教士重复了他从理发师和男孩士兵那里听到的信息,使他流泪。

他在家里苦苦地祈祷了一段时间,他首先想到,如果他接受基督,他将反对他所知道的所有建议和教导,更不用说整个犹太社区了。 但他最终确信耶稣确实是"旧约预言"的实现(特别是创世纪49:10,米迦5:2和以赛亚7:14).

他就祈祷说:易卜拉欣、易司哈格、叶尔孤白的主啊! 你知道我对这件事很真诚 如果耶稣基督是上帝之子,那么今晚把他告诉我,我将接受他为我的弥赛亚。” 一场漫长的战斗随之而来,但他的疑虑最终被欢乐和幸福所取代,因为他称赞上帝找到了真正的希洛,以色列统治者和埃马纽埃尔.

但他要付出高昂的代价,跟随基督的所有人一样。 他的妻子抛弃了他;他的父母抛弃了他。 但是,他从未放弃过希望,因为他不断祈祷和联系家人。 在54天后,他的妻子作为耶稣的门徒加入了他,在时间上,他的女儿也成为了信徒.

但他的儿子与他断绝关系多年,直到他最终与他的大地父和天父都和解. 在他来到基督的大约18个月之后的一段非凡续集中,马克思在战场上遇见了那些年前他死去的年轻病人的母亲科尔森夫人.

他怀着极大的喜悦,得以分享她儿子如何使他踏上基督辉煌未来的道路,这就是触摸世界各地的生活,包括我的家乡英格兰约克郡. 事实上,他来到利兹居住,向那里的犹太社区伸出援手,并被埋在城内的草坪林墓地.

我的一个爱尔兰朋友科林·内文参观了这个坟墓,其中包括医生颂歌"I am Coming Soon"的节录,并且能够把马克思的故事复制给看守人,因此在1892年去世后一个多世纪的福音派传承下来,享年64岁.

一部54分钟的电影 — — Rossvally: 从Synagogue到救世主 — 已经在DVD上制作,显然可以在网上订购. 在目睹病人的勇气首次出现在上帝的报告之后,
